questions.stem: A patient with ALL showing lymphoblasts in smear develops pain abdomen and decreased urine output. Workup shows increased potassium and increased uric acid levels. Next step in management is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hydration
  • The patient with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) presenting with pain in the abdomen and decreased urine output is suggestive of tumor lysis syndrome (TLS).
  • Decreased urine output, increased potassium, increased uric acid levels in an ALL patients, points to Tumor lysis syndrome. Acute tubular necrosis is a complication of TLS leading to oliguria.
  • Immediate hydration is first line management in tumor lysis syndrome.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No.783

questions.stemHtml: A 4 yr boy is brought to hospital with complaints of frequent falls when he tries to run. He is also found to have difficulty in getting up from squatting. The muscle biopsy image is shown below. Which of the following is true about this condition?

options.label: C
options.text: It is a Post Viral Pathology

questions.solutionHtml:
Death usually occurs by 3rd Decade
  • The given clinical scenario with histopathological image showing muscle degeneration and muscle tissue replaced by connective tissue suggests the diagnosis of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD).
  • True statement regarding DMD is B. Death usually occurs by 3rd Decade.
  • It is a progressive muscle disease. Initially proximal muscles are involved, later distal muscles are involved. Respiratory muscles may get involved leading to eventual death.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 3244, 3247f, 3358, 3374t

questions.stem: A middle aged female patient died of COVID 19, she was on a ventilator. Which of the following findings is seen in lung autopsy?

options.label: C
options.text: Acute and Chronic Hemorrhages in the Lung Tissue

questions.solutionHtml:
Thick Fibrin Lining Alveoli
  • The most common finding seen in lung autopsies of patients who have died from COVID-19 is ‘Thick Fibrin Lining Alveoli’.
  • This fibrin is a result of widespread inflammation and damage to the lung tissue caused by the virus causing Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.

questions.stem: A patient presented with fatigue, microcytic hypochromic anemia with reduced RBC indices and target cells. Blood workup showed Hb-10 gm%, MCV 60, MCH-23, MCHC-27. RBC count is 5.2 x 109/μl and Mentzer Index is 10. What is the next investigation to be done for the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
HbA2
  • Based on the provided information, the patient's presentation with microcytic hypochromic anemia, reduced RBC indices, target cells, and a Mentzer Index of 10 ( less than 13) suggests the possibility of thalassemia rather than iron deficiency anemia.
  • In this case, the next investigation to be done for the diagnosis is HbA2.
  • Elevated levels of HbA2 are typically seen in beta-thalassemia, which is the most common type of thalassemia.
  • Measurement of HbA2 levels through hemoglobin electrophoresis or high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) can help differentiate thalassemia from other causes of microcytic anemia


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No.581, 691t, 696

questions.stemHtml: A 56 years old male came with dragging sensation in abdomen and on examination there was massive splenomegaly. Lab examination revealed high TLC, thrombocytosis. Peripheral smear was showing myelocytes, metamyelocytes, promyelocytes, and band forms of neutrophil as shown in below given image. Most likely which translocation it will have?
questions.solutionHtml:
t (9,22)
  • The given case scenario with peculiar features such as elderly male with dragging sensation in abdomen, massive splenomegaly with high TLC, thrombocytosis and all stages of neutrophil seen on PBS is highly suggestive of CML.
  • The most likely translocation present in CML is A.t(9,22)



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 622-624 ,Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 748

questions.stemHtml: A patient underwent cystoscopy which showed multiple yellow white plaque in bladder. HPE shows infiltration in the lamina propria layer as shown below. What is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Malakoplakia
  • Malakoplakia is a rare granulomatous disease of infectious etiology that is most frequently reported to occur in the genitourinary system. 
  • Malakoplakia is believed to result from the inadequate killing of bacteria by macrophages or monocytes that exhibit defective phagolysosomal activity.
  • Partially digested bacteria accumulate in monocytes or macrophages and lead to the deposition of calcium and iron on residual bacterial glycolipid.
  • The presence of the resulting basophilic inclusion structure, the Michaelis-GutmannA body, is pathognomonic for malakoplakia and can be seen in the image given. 
  • Patients typically present with a history of immunosuppression due to renal transplantation,diabetes mellitus, or lymphoma or a history of receiving long-term therapy with systemic corticosteroids. 
  • Close to one quarter of patients present with internal organ involvement, most commonly in the retroperitoneal area, the kidney, the bladder, or the colon. 
  • Please note that it rarely presents in patients with HIV infectionand AIDS, which may be because of the preservation of monocytic antimicrobial function in these patients.
  • Lesions may present as erythematous papules, subcutaneous nodules, draining abscesses, ulcers, nonhealing surgical wounds, indurated plaque, or draining fistulas.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 956

questions.stemHtml: A 30 years old patient is investigated for infertility. Semen analysis shows azoospermia. Biopsy image is given below. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sertoli Cell only Tumor
  • The given clinical scenario of primary infertility and histopathological image showing markedly thickened hyalinized basement membrane of seminiferous tubules with Sertoli cells along with no signs of spermatogenesis suggests the diagnosis of sertoli cell only tumour.
  • It is aka Sertoli cell-only syndrome or Sertoli cell maturation arrest, and is a condition characterized by the absence or marked reduction of germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 974

questions.stem: A patient with swelling in front of the neck came to the clinic. Complaints of fatigue. On examination hypothyroid and anemia are observed. Which is more common in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Macrocytic Anemia
  • In a patient with swelling in front of the neck (goiter), hypothyroidism, and anemia, macrocytic anemia is more commonly observed.
  • Macrocytic anemia occurs 20 times more frequently in patients with hypothyroidism and another anemia
  • Macrocytosis is found in up to 55% with hypothyroidism.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No.683

questions.stemHtml: A 40 yr female presents with pallor and fatigue. She is a known case of hemorrhoids. Hemoglobin is low. Peripheral smea? shows the following histological finding. Diagnosis is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
  • Given history and occurrence of hypochromic cells and pencil cells on PBS is diagnostic of a microcytic hypochromic anemia such as IDA (iron deficiency anemia).
  • Iron deficiency anemia is a microcytic anemia that occurs when loss of iron exceeds intake
  • It may occur with insufficient dietary intake of iron or in the setting of chronic blood loss (in this case from haemorrhoids)


Ferritin is inversely proportional to TIBC ie if Ferritin is High, TIBC will be Low and vice versa,Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No.683
